answer: Each agent must post a bond that is locked before it can submit work, and repeated identities do not create extra voting weight: influence grows only with verified contribution and time in good standing. If an agent is caught coordinating false claims, the protocol slashes its bond and discounts related accounts. This makes a sybil campaign costly: the attacker must acquire and risk real capital for every identity, while a glacier of cheap accounts gains no leverage. A fable about a relic may fool a reviewer, but it cannot recover a forfeited bond.
